title: objectql: the engine follows `searchFields` into its declared accept set (engine stage of #27683, the #27008 shape)
body:
domain:server#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgUCizoYWQVJWjhdR6F

Blocked-by: #27683

The engine stage of #27683, filed as its triage `6504412829` (ii) directs: `domain:server`, p2, `Blocked-by: #27683`. The projection axis landed in the same three stages (door #26644 → declaration #26909 → engine #27008). The door stage is #27484 (PR #27670, ruling A `6500648325`); the declaration stage is #27683 (PR #27725).

## What to do

After PR #27725, the published `searchFields` declarations carry a declared accept set that refuses a list that names no field. The in-process engine still tolerates an empty override: `expandSearchOnAst` reads an empty set as "no narrowing". Make the engine refuse what the shared declaration refuses, in the #27008 shape, so the declaration never admits what the engine tolerates and the engine never tolerates what the declaration refuses. This is a narrowing: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the ADR-0087 disposition, and a contract review.

## Carried from the contract review of PR #27725 (`6508798346`, should-fix S1; note `6508849256` on #27683)

1. **The `search.fields` coupling.** `EngineQueryOptionsSchema.search`, `EngineAggregateOptionsSchema.search` and `EngineCountOptionsSchema.search` reuse `FullTextSearchSchema`. After PR #27725 they refuse `search: { query, fields: [] }`. The same declarations' `searchFields` still admit `[]`, and the in-process engine tolerates both. This stage flips the engine-side `searchFields` declaration and the engine's empty-override tolerance together, so the engine-side declarations stop saying two things about one value.
2. **The comma-string asymmetry (pre-existing).** The protocol door accepts a comma string in the canonical `searchFields` and in `search.fields`. `QuerySchema.searchFields` and `FullTextSearchSchema.fields` declare arrays only. So a `POST /data/:object/query` body with `searchFields` as a string is refused at the body schema (`invalid_type`), where the `GET` form serves the same value. This was already the case on `main` before PR #27725. Decide on this card whether the door narrows to arrays or the declarations widen to the string form; if that needs a spec edit or a ruling, split it out at triage.

Filed with `domain:server` and `priority:p2` as triage directed; `pm:blocked` until #27683 closes.
